chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension with metabolic syndrome and frequent emergency visits for pain and substance‑use complications.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 39‑year‑old man with longstanding essential hypertension, obesity, sleep apnea, prediabetes, chronic intractable migraine and chronic pain. Blood pressure remains in the stage 2 range (136/93 mmHg) despite lisinopril 10 mg daily. He has ongoing dependent drug abuse, multiple emergency department visits, and limited outpatient follow‑up since 2018. Social determinants such as unstable housing, low education, social isolation, and high‑risk behaviors further impede disease management. No recent labs for lipids, renal function, or BMI are available, and there is no documented treatment for sleep apnea or migraine.
past_medical_history: Resolved overdoses (2017, 2018), prior medication review due (resolved 2018-10-23), previous part‑time employment, prior documented stress episode, and earlier full‑time employment (resolved 2016-10-11).
social_determinants: Housing unsatisfactory, only primary school education, limited social contact, social isolation, dependent drug abuse, involvement in high‑risk activities, full‑time employment with associated stress.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 136/93 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension), BMI documented as obesity (BMI ≥ 30) but exact value missing, A1c 6.1% (prediabetic). Charlson comorbidity index 1, clinical complexity moderate, polypharmacy risk low. Comorbidity flags: hypertension, anemia. Elevated risk across cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes), metabolic (prediabetes, obesity), respiratory/sleep (obstructive sleep apnea), hematologic (anemia), and psychosocial domains (substance abuse, unstable housing, low education, social isolation).
